title: Condition Adjustment for Unrepaired Earlier Damage on a Total Loss
content:
**Rule.** Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), unrepaired earlier damage is taken off the vehicle value paid to a loss payee as a condition adjustment.

**What counts as earlier damage.** It is the repair payments made to the named insured on the coverage's earlier claims, plus the deductibles taken from those payments.
- Only payments made to the named insured count, meaning paid out in cash and not to a repair facility.
- Earlier claims are every claim on the coverage other than the claim being settled.

**How much is taken off.**
- When the earlier damage is no more than the condition-adjustment cap share of 0.25 (25 percent) of the actual cash value on the total loss declaration, the whole earlier damage is taken off.
- When it is more, only that 25 percent share of the declared actual cash value is taken off.
- When there is no earlier damage, nothing is taken off.

### Hypothetical cases (declared actual cash value 12,400.00 USD, so the 25 percent share is 3,100.00 USD)

| Earlier claims on the coverage | Earlier damage | Taken off |
|---|---|---|
| One cash repair payment of 1,840.00 USD with 500.00 USD deductible taken | 2,340.00 USD | 2,340.00 USD |
| Cash payments of 3,150.00 USD with 450.00 USD deductibles taken | 3,600.00 USD | 3,100.00 USD |
| A repair payment made to a repair facility only | None | Nothing |
| No earlier claim | None | Nothing |
